title: Obligation and Compulsion in the Past

sections.title: Obliged and Forced
sections.content: You know *köteles* and *kénytelen* from B1 Unit 10. In a past account they take *volt*: *a társaság köteles volt üzemeltetni a megrendelt vonatokat*, *a MÁV kénytelen volt felfüggeszteni a forgalmat*. *Köteles* names a duty laid down by a rule or contract; *kénytelen* names a lack of choice.

sections.title: Whose Reasoning
sections.content: A *kénytelen volt* sentence gives the reasoning of one side, so it needs its source: *a kormány indoklása szerint … kénytelen volt …*. With a plural subject the adjective agrees: *a lakosok kénytelenek voltak*.

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: A társaság köteles volt üzemeltetni a megrendelt vonatokat.
The company was obliged to operate the trains that had been ordered.
A MÁV indoklása szerint a társaság kénytelen volt felfüggeszteni a forgalmat.
According to MÁV's reasoning, the company was forced to suspend the service.
Az önkormányzatok szerint a lakosok kénytelenek voltak buszra szállni.
According to the local governments, the residents were forced to take a bus.
